text:
ana: heads up — vuln scanner flagged CVE-2026-1901 (glibc) in our base image lineage (ubuntu:20.04 -> rwi-base:v2). Severity: high. I think we need a coordinated base image rebuild + runtime mitigations.

morgan: ack. can you paste the scanner output?

ana: here —
```
VULN: CVE-2026-1901
Package: libc6
Affected image: rwi-base:v2 (derived from ubuntu:20.04)
Severity: HIGH
Fix: libc6 2.31-0ubuntu9.9 or later
Scan: image-scan-2026-04-01
```

josh: re: immediate mitigations — we should enforce runtime policies so any pod using old image can't escalate. Suggested short list: drop ALL capabilities, read-only root fs, no-new-privs, seccomp profile, user namespace.

lia: +1. Also need to ensure our image signing + KMS rotation is in the loop. If we rebuild images, they must be cosigned using our key in KMS (key-id: projects/redwood/keys/image-signing). Who owns the cosign job?

sam: I can own the cosign pipeline. Quick Q: does cosign use the same KMS key as terraform/state encryption? We need separate key for signing ideally.

ana: yes separate key. Security recommends: KMS key with limited IAM: only cosign-service-account + infra-admins can useAsymmetricSign. Add key rotation every 90d.

morgan: RBAC change needed: we must prevent the build service account from pushing to stable repo until rebuilt images pass vuln scan. Proposal: create a new repo tag `staging-rebuild` and only allow `ci-builder` to push there; `release-bot` will only pull when scan passes. Need policy snippet.

josh: policy sketch (kubernetes ImageRegistry role bindings):
```
- role: image-pusher
  subjects: ["system:serviceaccount:ci:ci-builder"]
  resources: ["staging-rebuild/*"]
- role: image-promoter
  subjects: ["system:serviceaccount:infra:release-bot"]
  condition: scan_pass == true
```

lia: also wire audit logging to store image-push events to our long-term audit cluster (retention 2y) so compliance can prove images were signed and scanned. We need an event shim that records: image, digest, signer_key, scan_report_id.

devsec-bot: AUTO: created ticket INC-4827 in incidents for base-image rebuild coordination. Assigned: sam, josh. SLA: 72h for rollout to hosted and dedicated.

ana: timeline idea:
- T+0: freeze stable pushes (apply RBAC block) — 30m
- T+2h: kick off rebuild pipeline for all images referencing rwi-base:v2 (job: rebuild-base-1764) — triggers CI, vuln-scan, cosign
- T+8h: smoke test + canary rollout to a subset of infra (10% traffic) with runtime hardening flags enforced — if green, promote
- T+24-72h: full rollout depending on canary results

morgan: for runtime security flags, include these in our pod template generator:
```
securityContext:
  runAsNonRoot: true
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  capabilities:
    drop: ["ALL"]
```
Also attach a standard `runtime-seccomp.json` profile from our secops repo.

josh: note: some infra services (logging/monitoring sidecars) break with read-only fs. We'll add an annotation `rwi.security/allow-fs-write: true` but require a justified ticket + sec review. Keep the exception list small.

lia: KMS integration checklist for cosign pipeline:
- ensure cosign uses KMS asymmetric keys (OIDC service account)
- add IAM binding: roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier to cosign SA only
- log key usage to audit logs to separate GCP project (for e-discovery)
- automate key rotation and update cosign config (rotation window 90d)

ana: vuln triage: we validated that runtime mitigation reduces exploitability surface but not a substitute for rebuild. Prioritizing rebuild because upstream fix exists. Marking as P0 for base images.

sam: I'll create the rebuild job `rebuild-base-1764` today and link to the CI job. Starting with these repos: `rwi/runtime`, `rwi/sidecars`, `rwi/ingress`.

morgan: who can run the canary? I'll need a short runbook so oncall can execute rollback quickly. Lia, can you draft a rollback step with commands?

lia: sure. draft rollback snippet:
```
# promote previous digest back to stable
gcloud artifacts docker images add-tag --project=redwood-repo rwi/runtime@sha256:<old> rwi/runtime:stable --quiet
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime -n prod
# revoke cosign trust for the new digest if needed
cosign remove-claim --key ksm://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/images/cryptoKeys/image-signing <sha>
```
Will flesh out the full runbook in the incident ticket.

josh: quick question on audit logging — retention 2y is fine, but we should also export to the SIEM (splunk) within 1h for alerting on unsigned-image-push. Lia, can you own the SIEM hook?

lia: yes. I'll add a Cloud Audit Logs sink to send image-push audit entries to splunk and to our long-term bucket.

ana: OK action items summary (short):
- sam: create rebuild pipeline + cosign integration (INC-4827) — owner
- josh: update pod templates & exception process + help with canary analysis — co-owner
- lia: audit logging sink + sec runbook + KMS bindings — owner
- morgan: RBAC policy to block stable pushes until signed scans pass — owner
- ana: coordinate communications with product + customer success for any user-impacting incidents — owner

morgan: adding a small automation: if scan fails, create a blocker label on the repo and open an auto-PR to pin to previous secure digest. Can we do that?

sam: yes we can. I'll add a `scan-gate` in the CI with an auto-PR flow.

devsec-bot: UPDATE: INC-4827 status set to "in-progress". Linked PR: github.com/redwood/rebuilds/pull/92

ana: thanks all. I'll post a short note in #incident-ops and schedule a 30m sync in 15m to go over blockers. If you see any service anomalies after canary, tag #incidents and ping @oncall. :thumbsup:

lia: added initial runbook draft to INC-4827 and notified compliance.

josh: I'll start drafting the RBAC change in infra repo and include the policy tests.

sam: starting rebuild job now. will update thread with scan results.

ana: perfect. closing the thread for updates; please keep replies in the ticket.
